surface_mechanism_description: Surface reactions governing the growth of CdTe were studied using Auger electron spectroscopy (AES). Deposition was terminated alternately at Cd and Te, and the Cd/Te peak-to-peak ratio of the principal Cd MNN and Te MNN Auger transitions was measured after every pulse. The Cd/Te ratio appeared always 10%-15% greater for the (111) A face than for the (111) B face. The sticking coefficients of Cd and Te suffer an abrupt change from about 1 to 0 at the full monolayer coverage. A stable Cd to Te bond is formed by subjecting the surface to a Te2 pulse until all the bonds are completed.
